prompt.context_jp: まず耳に届くのは、この組織の綱領を語る都知事・赤塚梓の声である。
prompt.prompt_jp: まず耳に届くの___、この組織の綱領を語る都知事・赤塚梓の声である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「耳に届くの」.

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized 「耳に届くの」 is the topic/frame being described, and the predicate identifies WHAT it is (Akatsuka's voice). は works as the topic marker in this のは…である cleft-like structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 「耳に届くの」 into new information needing identification, but here it is the frame; を is impossible since there is no transitive verb taking it.

contrast_examples.jp: 聞こえるのは鳥の声だ。
contrast_examples.en: What's audible is the sound of birds.
A bird's voice can be heard.

prompt.context_jp: 報告を受けているのは、ＭＥＲの解散を虎視眈々と狙う与党幹事長・白金眞理子である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 報告を受けているのは、ＭＥＲの解散___虎視眈々と狙う与党幹事長・白金眞理子である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「ＭＥＲの解散」.

feedback.correct_en: 狙う ('to aim/target') takes a direct object, so 解散 is marked with を — she is targeting MER's dissolution.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 解散 the subject (something aims at her), which inverts the meaning. に would suggest direction, not the thing targeted.

contrast_examples.en: To aim for the next victory.
He is being targeted.

prompt.context_jp: 白金：「現場を見て分かったんだけど あのチームは喜多見が全て」
prompt.prompt_jp: あのチーム___喜多見が全て。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「あのチーム」.

feedback.correct_en: Shirakane is making a judgment about 'that team' as the topic — what she will say about it is that Kitami is everything. は sets the team as the frame; が then exhaustively identifies Kitami as 'the all' within that frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using が on チーム would stack two subjects without a topic frame and lose the 'as for that team…' nuance that makes this diagnosis land.

contrast_examples.jp: この店はラーメンが一番だ。
contrast_examples.en: As for this shop, ramen is the best.

contrast_examples.jp: この店がラーメンで有名だ。
contrast_examples.en: It's this shop that is famous for ramen.

prompt.context_jp: 音羽：「与党の幹事長ににらまれ ＭＥＲは いつ潰されても おかしくない状況です 皆さん 危機感___なさすぎます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆さん 危機感___なさすぎます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「危機感」.

feedback.correct_en: With adjectival predicates like なさすぎる describing an attribute, が marks what there is 'too little of'. The topic 皆さん is already set; 危機感 is the new focused attribute.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would create double-topic awkwardness and weaken the diagnostic punch. を doesn't fit because なさすぎる isn't a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はやる気がなさすぎる。
contrast_examples.en: He has far too little motivation.
Motivation, (he) has.

prompt.context_jp: 音羽：「今は 喜多見チーフという 規格外の存在がいるから うまくいってるだけですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今は 喜多見チーフという 規格外の存在___いるから うまくいってるだけですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「規格外の存在」.

feedback.correct_en: Existence verbs (いる/ある) take が when introducing or asserting the presence of the entity — here 'the fact that there IS such an exceptional person' is the new information fueling the reason-clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into contrast/topic ('as for an exceptional person…') and lose the causal 'because such a person exists' force. に marks location/target, not the existing entity itself.

contrast_examples.en: There is a cat in the room.
The cat is in the room (as for the cat).

prompt.context_jp: 死者を一人も出さないようにするというチームの誓いは、数字の上では見事に守られている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 死者を一人も出さないようにするというチームの誓い___、数字の上では見事に守られている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「チームの誓い」.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up the team's vow as the topic and then evaluates how it is being held up. は marks this known, already-introduced theme that the predicate comments on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the vow as newly identified information, but by this point in the report it's an established concept being evaluated, not newly introduced.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の約束は守られている。
contrast_examples.en: His promise is being kept (as for it).
The moment a promise was kept (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 駆け寄ってきたのはレスキュー隊の駒場卓であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 駆け寄ってきたの___レスキュー隊の駒場卓であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「駆け寄ってきたの」.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft-style 「〜のは…だ」 structure: 'The one who ran up WAS Komaba.' The nominalized clause is the topic frame, and the identifying NP comes after.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would double up as a subject on a clause already functioning as a presentational topic, breaking the cleft reading.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was Tanaka.
Tanaka came (new info).

prompt.context_jp: そのとき無線が鳴り、目黒の声が新たな情報を告げてくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのとき無線___鳴り、目黒の声が新たな情報を告げてくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「無線」.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event verb like 鳴る introducing new information in a narrative scene takes が — the radio ringing is a fresh happening on stage.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 無線 as an already-known topic being commented on, which doesn't fit this sudden event. に is directional, not for the ringing entity.

contrast_examples.en: The phone rang (sudden event).
The phone (as topic) didn't ring.

prompt.context_jp: 比奈：「右の呼吸音が聞こえません 恐らく 右の緊張性気胸です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 右の呼吸音___聞こえません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「右の呼吸音」.

feedback.correct_en: Perception verbs like 聞こえる take が on the thing perceived (or not perceived). Hina is reporting a fresh clinical finding — the right breath sound is absent.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would contrast ('the right one isn't, [but the left is]') which sounds like deliberate comparison rather than a clinical observation. を doesn't go with the intransitive 聞こえる.

contrast_examples.en: A sound is audible.
The sound (in particular) isn't audible.

prompt.context_jp: 兄の並外れた腕に頼ってばかりでは、この組織はいずれ崩れるかもしれない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 兄の並外れた腕に頼ってばかりでは、この組織___いずれ崩れるかもしれない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「この組織」.

feedback.correct_en: The organization has been the ongoing theme of Suzuka's worry; the sentence states a general prediction ABOUT it. は carries this topical, judgment-like reading.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 「この組織」 as freshly discovered subject, but it's the established frame of her concern — a general prediction, not a scene-level event.

contrast_examples.jp: この会社はいずれ潰れる。
contrast_examples.en: This company will eventually collapse.
A/the company collapsed (event).

prompt.context_jp: 音羽：「我々は 喜多見チーフのように 特殊な人間ではないですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 我々___ 喜多見チーフのように 特殊な人間ではないですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「我々」.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa is contrasting 'us' with Chief Kitami. は carries both the topic and the contrastive reading — 'we, unlike him, aren't exceptional.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely identify the subject without the contrastive sting. も ('also/even we') contradicts the intended distinction from Kitami.

contrast_examples.en: I (as opposed to others) am not special.
I (exhaustively) am the special one.

prompt.context_jp: 最初に手をつけた徳丸元一が、口をもぐもぐさせながら短い感想を漏らす。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初に手をつけた徳丸元一___、口をもぐもぐさせながら短い感想を漏らす。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「徳丸元一」.

feedback.correct_en: Tokumaru is being newly introduced into this narrative scene with a modifying clause 'the first to take a bite'. が marks the fresh participant entering the stage.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require Tokumaru to already be the established topic being discussed, but the narrative is zooming in on him as a new scene participant.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の男が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: A man came in (new on scene).
The man (established) stayed silent.

prompt.context_jp: だが今回の山は広く、傷病者がどこに散らばっているのかさえ、まだ誰にも分かっていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが今回の山___広く、傷病者がどこに散らばっているのかさえ、まだ誰にも分かっていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「今回の山」.

feedback.correct_en: だが signals a contrast to the previous norm. 今回の山 is the new topic being compared against prior cases — 'this time, the mountain is vast'. は carries both topic and the implicit contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just assert a bare fact without picking up the contrastive flow from だが. に would mark location, which doesn't fit the predicate 広い.

contrast_examples.en: Today (as opposed to usually) is cold.
Today is the coldest (exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: ＥＲカーは轟音を上げて奥多摩へ向かう高速道路を疾走する。
prompt.prompt_jp: ＥＲカーは轟音を上げて奥多摩へ向かう高速道路___疾走する。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「高速道路」.

feedback.correct_en: Motion verbs like 疾走する mark the PATH traversed with を — the highway is the route being raced along.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the highway merely as the location where an action happens, losing the sense of racing ALONG it. に marks destination, not route.

contrast_examples.en: Run along the road.
Play on the road (location).

prompt.context_jp: 沈黙のあと、音羽が短く息を吸って一歩前に出た。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沈黙のあと、音羽___短く息を吸って一歩前に出た。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「音羽」.

feedback.correct_en: A new participant stepping forward out of silence is a scene-level event. が marks Otowa as the newly spotlighted actor emerging from the previously discussed group.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Otowa as a continuing topic being commented on, but the sentence captures a sudden visual beat — he, specifically, moves.

contrast_examples.en: He stood up (event).
He (as topic) stayed silent.

prompt.context_jp: 重い沈黙を破ったのは、木々の間から聞こえてくる低いモーター音だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 重い沈黙を破ったの___、木々の間から聞こえてくる低いモーター音だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「重い沈黙を破ったの」.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft 「〜のは…だった」: the frame 'what broke the heavy silence' is given, and the identifying NP (motor sound) comes after. は marks the cleft topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が on a nominalized のだ-type clause would double up on subject marking and break the cleft structure the narration is using for suspense.

contrast_examples.jp: 沈黙を破ったのは一本の電話だった。
contrast_examples.en: What broke the silence was a single phone call.
A phone call broke the silence (plain event).

prompt.context_jp: 白金：「記者を張りつかせて 喜多見を____ましょう 過去が分からなくても スキャンダルの1つや2つ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見を____ましょう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits — Shirakane is ordering a dig into Kitami's background.

feedback.correct_en: 「〜を洗う」 is an idiomatic/underworld-flavored expression meaning 'to investigate someone's background thoroughly'. It fits Shirakane's cold, scheming tone perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流す means to let flow/wash away — the opposite of digging up dirt. 拭く means wipe clean, also opposite of investigating.

contrast_examples.en: To investigate someone's background.
To let the past wash away (forget).

prompt.context_jp: 白金：「____にしよう」(team-splitting plot)
prompt.prompt_jp: ____にしよう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that captures Shirakane's intent — scattering/breaking up the team.

feedback.correct_en: バラバラにする means to break something unified into scattered pieces — exactly her plan to split MER apart.
feedback.incorrect_en: ゆっくり ('slowly') and きれい ('clean/pretty') don't convey breaking a group apart.

contrast_examples.jp: 家族がバラバラになる。
contrast_examples.en: The family gets split apart.
To make the room clean.

prompt.context_jp: 音羽：「ありがとうございます お____だけ頂きます」(declining a gift politely)
prompt.prompt_jp: お____だけ頂きます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that forms the polite 'I'll take just your (X)' refusal.

feedback.correct_en: 「お気持ちだけ頂きます」 is a fixed polite refusal: 'I accept your sentiment/thought (but not the gift itself)'. It softens the decline.
feedback.incorrect_en: お考え and お心 are not fixed in this refusal frame — they'd sound odd or over-literal in this context.

contrast_examples.jp: お気持ちだけ頂戴します。
contrast_examples.en: I'll gratefully accept just your kind thought.

contrast_examples.jp: お気持ちはよく分かります。
contrast_examples.en: I understand your feelings well.

prompt.context_jp: 「百聞は____にしかず 見せてください」
prompt.prompt_jp: 百聞は____にしかず。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 「百聞は一見にしかず」 ('Seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times') is a fixed proverb — ask to actually see the photo rather than hear about it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一回 and 一度 both mean 'one time' but neither forms this classical set phrase.

contrast_examples.en: A picture is worth a thousand words.

contrast_examples.jp: もう一度見せてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please show me once more.

prompt.context_jp: 白金：「ついに見られるわね ＭＥＲの____の皮が 剥がれる瞬間が」
prompt.prompt_jp: ＭＥＲの____の皮が剥がれる瞬間。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that forms this idiom about a false front being exposed.

feedback.correct_en: 「化けの皮が剥がれる」 is a set phrase meaning 'the mask falls / true nature is exposed'. Shirakane savors the moment MER's facade will crumble.
feedback.incorrect_en: 本当の皮 and 顔の皮 are not fixed idioms. The nuance of unmasking requires 化け (disguise/pretense).

contrast_examples.en: The disguise is torn off.
One's true identity is exposed.

prompt.context_jp: 音羽：「運ぶ時間が ____になるかもしれません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 運ぶ時間が ____になるかもしれません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits — the carrying time could prove fatal.

feedback.correct_en: 命取り means 'something that costs a life / a fatal factor'. Transport time becoming lethal is exactly this nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 命拾い means to narrowly escape death — the opposite. 命がけ means 'risking one's life' and modifies effort, not time.

contrast_examples.jp: 一瞬の油断が命取りになる。
contrast_examples.en: A moment's carelessness can be fatal.
To fight with one's life on the line.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見：「現場に判断を____ます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 現場に判断を____ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb — Kitami entrusts on-site decisions to the teams.

feedback.correct_en: 「判断を委ねる」 is the standard collocation for entrusting a decision to someone else's judgment — leaving it in their hands.
feedback.incorrect_en: 預ける is for depositing physical/temporary custody (bags, children). 渡す means literal handover, not entrusting authority.

contrast_examples.en: To entrust the decision to a subordinate.
To deposit luggage.

prompt.context_jp: 徳丸：「お____御用っすよ てか これ 使ってみたかったんで」
prompt.prompt_jp: お____御用っすよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the casual 'no problem / easy favor' expression.

feedback.correct_en: 「お安い御用」 is a set phrase meaning 'an easy favor / no sweat'. Tokumaru brushes off thanks casually.
feedback.incorrect_en: お軽い御用 and お小さい御用 aren't idiomatic — only 安い works in this fixed expression.

contrast_examples.en: That's an easy favor (no problem).
It's nothing much.

prompt.context_jp: Chief Kitami argues for immediate action over waiting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Kitami's decisive, urgent declaration?

choices.text: 待っていたら 助けられない命もある
もし待てば 助けられない命がときどきある
待つなら いくつかの命は助けられない

feedback.correct_en: The source line uses たら + 〜もある for a punchy, emotionally weighted claim: 'if we wait, there are also lives that can't be saved.' Compact and natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's ときどきある softens it into a frequency statement, undermining the urgency. C's 待つなら…いくつかの sounds like a stiff translation and misses the 〜もある emphasis.

contrast_examples.jp: 急がないと間に合わないこともある。
contrast_examples.en: If we don't hurry, there are times we won't make it.

contrast_examples.jp: 急がなければ、ときどき間に合わない。
contrast_examples.en: If we don't hurry, sometimes we won't make it (flat).

prompt.context_jp: Hina realizes 20 minutes is too long for the boy to survive transport.
prompt.prompt_en: Which rendering sounds most natural as Hina's tense in-the-moment reaction?

choices.text: それじゃ間に合わない
それでは時間に合わないでしょう
そうすると時刻に遅れます

feedback.correct_en: In an emergency, the clipped 「それじゃ間に合わない」 (plain form, 間に合う = make it in time) is natural, urgent, and colloquial.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 時間に合わない is unnatural Japanese (間に合う is the fixed collocation). C's 時刻に遅れる refers to being late to a scheduled time, not failing to save someone in time.

contrast_examples.jp: 急がないと間に合わない。
contrast_examples.en: We won't make it if we don't hurry.
I made the train in time.

prompt.context_jp: Otowa scolds Min for dashing off alone in the field.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Otowa's sharp admonition to a junior?

choices.text: ミンさん 勝手に行動しないで
ミンさん 自由に行動するのをやめてください
ミンさん 一人で動くのは禁止ですよ

feedback.correct_en: 「勝手に〜ないで」 is the natural Japanese way to tell someone 'don't act on your own (without permission)'. It carries the right scolding-senpai tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 自由に行動する sounds like discussing a right/freedom rather than unauthorized action. C's 禁止 is overly bureaucratic for an in-the-moment rebuke.

contrast_examples.en: Don't decide on your own.
You can move freely.

prompt.context_jp: Tokumaru explains that engineers also save lives.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as Tokumaru's casual assertion?

choices.text: 命を救うのは 医者や看護師だけじゃないんで
命を救うことは 医者と看護師しかできないわけではないので
医者や看護師が命を救う唯一の人ではありません

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 〜のは…だけじゃない delivers a punchy, spoken-register claim — exactly Tokumaru's slightly cocky style with 〜んで at the end.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatical but wordy and stiff. C sounds like translated English — Japanese rarely uses 唯一の人 in casual speech.

contrast_examples.jp: 勉強するのは学生だけじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: Students aren't the only ones who study.

contrast_examples.jp: 学生のみが勉強するわけではない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not that only students study (stiff).

prompt.context_jp: A senior figure chews out a subordinate for daring to submit a report that praises MER.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a sneering, blunt rebuke to Kugayama?

choices.text: お前 よく こんな報告書 出せたな
あなたは このような報告書を提出することができましたね
君は この報告書を上手に出しました

feedback.correct_en: The sarcastic 「よく〜できたな」 with お前 and dropped particles is natural rough-superior speech expressing disbelief/disapproval — 'you've got some nerve submitting this'.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite and literal, losing the sarcasm. C praises the report instead of attacking it — misreading the tone entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: よくそんなこと言えたな。
contrast_examples.en: How dare you say something like that.
Well done! (sincere praise)
